questions.prompt: Write `Evens(max)` so it **lazily** yields 0, 2, 4, … up to and including `max`. The last test asks for the first three evens up to `int.MaxValue`, so it must not build a list first.
questions.explanation: `yield return` turns the method into an iterator: nothing runs until someone enumerates it, and each value is produced on demand, so Take(3) stops after three. Using a long counter also avoids `i += 2` overflowing past int.MaxValue.

questions.prompt: Write `CountLetters(text)`: how many times each letter appears, case-insensitively (as lowercase keys). Ignore anything that isn't a letter.
questions.explanation: `counts[key]++` throws KeyNotFoundException for a new key, so read with GetValueOrDefault (or TryGetValue) and write back. Use ToLowerInvariant so the result doesn't depend on the machine's culture.

questions.prompt: Using LINQ, write `TotalsByCustomer(orders)`: each customer's total order value.
questions.helpers: public record Order(string Customer, int Total);

tests.call: TotalsByCustomer(new[] { new Order("Ada", 10), new Order("Bo", 5), new Order("Ada", 7) })

questions.explanation: GroupBy gives one group per customer and ToDictionary turns each group into key → sum. `ToDictionary(o => o.Customer, ...)` without grouping first throws on the duplicate key "Ada".

questions.prompt: Write a generic `MaxBy(items, key)` that returns the item with the largest key (the first one on a tie), and throws `InvalidOperationException` when `items` is empty. Don't use LINQ's built-in MaxBy.

tests.call: try { MaxBy(new string[0], s => s.Length); return "no exception"; } catch (InvalidOperationException) { return "InvalidOperationException"; }

questions.explanation: Start from the first item rather than a sentinel like 0 or int.MinValue, so all-negative keys work and an empty sequence is detected. Enumerating once (instead of calling Any() then looping) also works for sequences that can only be read once.

questions.prompt: Write `IsPalindrome(s)`: true if `s` reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and anything that isn't a letter or digit.

tests.call: IsPalindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama")

questions.explanation: Two pointers from both ends, skipping characters that don't count: O(n) with no extra string. "0P" catches solutions that only keep letters (dropping the digit 0).
